analysis.title: "Leaving Vapor Trails": Nomura's McElligott Says Monday's Melt-Up Was A Vanna Machine, And The Machine Just Stalled
key_insights: Nomura's McElligott says Monday's (Nov 9) rally was driven mostly by a vol crush that forced dealers to buy back short futures hedges. 424 S&P 500 members closed higher vs 79 decliners (84% of the index).

VIX fell from 28 to 20 in about 2.5 sessions, a drop of almost 30%. Dealers were short customer-bought puts and OTM puts after last Thursday's equity crash. As spot rose and vol fell, the puts lost delta twice, once from spot and once from the vol input, and dealers bought back futures hedges (vanna).
Calls bought for a bounce moved closer to the money as spot rallied, forcing further dealer delta buying. McElligott describes the result as 'vapor trails'.
Tuesday morning the vol decline stalled and the stock rally stalled with it, since the forced dealer buying ended. October CPI then printed hot.
October CPI printed 0.4% MoM vs 0.3% expected, core 0.3% vs 0.2% expected. Only 1 of 70 analysts forecast it. Odds of a 50bp December hike rose to 14%.

Fed Governor Waller said in a London speech that he could support a 50bp hike in December if October inflation printed hot, which moved December pricing to 'fully priced' per McElligott. A +26k Tuesday weekly 10Y put buy on Monday, against prior open interest of 1,080, acted as hot-CPI insurance.

Rates vol 'got absolutely REKT' on Monday on the oil collapse, Iran terms moving closer and the clearing of election risk. Real money has tilted to selling further out the curve and receivers lost momentum. Investors will not pay for long vol or long gamma after poor performance.

Nomura's dashboard shows 1-month S&P realized vol at 22.1 (100th percentile) vs 14.7 for 3-month. Last Thursday's 4.4% drop stays in the 1-month window for weeks, so vol control funds cannot add risk. Their implied equity allocation fell to $116.1B (11.2 percentile over 3 years) from $124.6B.

Levered ETFs are a $142B complex (94th percentile) that must trade about $6.5B of stock per 1% move in the underlying. Rolling 1-month net flows are -$82.6B, the lowest on record, while creations alone are +$10.5B (100th percentile), meaning retail bought the dip with leverage.

10- and 20-day realized vol of VVIX are at record highs over a 10-year lookback (288.8 and 218.5), above COVID, Liberation Day and Volmageddon. McElligott credits the observation to MRA's Dean Curnutt and reads VVIX as a proxy for demand for wings and tails.

McElligott accepts the backtest that says to sell rich vol but argues the distribution of outcomes is widening because of questions over AI capex and its effect on nominal GDP, equity vol, skew, correlation, rates and credit. He suggests moving to a wider straddle and expects the VIX floor to rise.
Goldman's Rich Privorotsky had said 'Core at 0.2% would be constructive; 0.3% would challenge the rally.' Core printed 0.3%.
